help.help:
{~text align=center}{REFERENCE 1/2}} 

This dialog configures the object generators used by the random map generator. The pages are: common map objects, learning objects, income and resources, Creature Banks, creature dwellings, prisons and quests, WoG objects, treasures and Pandora's Boxes.

For ordinary generators, the JSON path is "RMG.objectGeneration.[type].[subtype]". The supported fields are enabled, value, density, map, zone, name and object-specific extension fields. Values from JSON become defaults; values changed in this dialog are saved to Runtime/RMG_CustomizeObjectsProperties.ini.

The Creature Banks page follows the detailed key and behavior reference on its page. Pandora's Boxes and prisons expose separate generator variants even when the game uses the same real subtype. Use the page-specific help for their variant rules.

pages.help:
{~text align=center}{Creature Bank Help}}:
The CreatureBanksExtender reads Creature Bank configuration from the JSON path "RMG.objectGeneration.<type>.<subtype>". For original banks use type 16 and the bank subtype; special banks use their object type and subtype 0. Missing keys keep the game or plugin defaults. Array indexes are zero-based.

Common object keys:
"name" - custom name of the bank.
"troopPlacement.isBank" - when false, use a regular monster battle instead of Creature Bank placement.
"troopPlacement.attackers.0..6" and "troopPlacement.defenders.0..6" - seven battlefield cells for each side. Valid cells are 1..186; blocked border cells are ignored.

Each bank has four states, "states.0" through "states.3". The state selected by its "chance" value is used when the bank is initialized.

State keys:
"customDef" - Adventure Map DEF name for this state.
"artifactTypeCounts.0..3" - number of random artifacts by the game's four rarity categories (indexes 0..3).
"artifactIds.0..3" - exact artifact IDs added to the reward.
"resources.0..7" - resource amounts in the order wood, ore, mercury, sulfur, crystals, gems, gold and mithril.
"creatureRewardType" and "creatureRewardCount" - creature ID and count for the creature reward.
"guardians.type.0..6" and "guardians.count.0..6" - seven guard stacks and their counts.
"upgrade" - upgrade chance (0..100) for the creature reward.
"chance" - probability of selecting this state (0..100); configure the state probabilities as a complete set.
"skills.primary.0..3" - attack, defense, spell power and knowledge bonuses.
"experience" - experience granted after plundering; Learning skill modifies the final amount.
"spellPoints" - spell points granted, capped by the hero's maximum.
"luck" and "morale" - bonuses clamped to -3..3.
"revealRadius" - radius revealed for the hero after the battle and when the reward is opened.

Spell rewards use four slots, "spells.0" through "spells.3":
"spells.<n>.id" gives an exact spell ID. If it is present, the bit filters for that slot are ignored.
Alternatively, omit "id" and set any of:
"spells.<n>.bits.schools" - school bit mask: Air=1, Fire=2, Water=4, Earth=8; combine flags with bitwise OR.
"spells.<n>.bits.levels" - level bit mask; level L is selected with (1 << L), so levels 2 and 3 use 4+8=12.
"spells.<n>.bits.flags" - spell flags bit mask matched against the spell's flags.
A slot with bit filters selects one eligible, non-banned and non-duplicate spell. The hero still needs a spellbook and sufficient Wisdom when the reward is given.

Optional text overrides:
"text.visit", "text.victory" and "text.plundered" replace the corresponding visit, victory and plundered messages for the selected bank.

The dialog's Value/Map/Zone/Density fields control the RMG object generator. Creature Bank reward fields above are read from the bank JSON and are applied when the bank is initialized; they are not substitutes for the four RMG object fields.

pages.help:
{Help on WoG objects}:
WoG objects (type 63) are also added via json, but all their mechanics are scripted (for now). Before including an object in generation, make sure that the corresponding object has a script or other implementation. Otherwise, an empty object will appear on the map, which will "eat" part of the value of the zone.
